newsitem.title: UK: UK store card accounts up 20 pct in yr to Sept-BRC.
newsitem.headline: UK store card accounts up 20 pct in yr to Sept-BRC.

text.p: The number of credit accounts held by UK retailers rose by 20 percent in the year to the end of September, the British Retail Consortium said on Monday.
The average amount owed on each account was 166 pounds, up less than one percent, the BRC said.

With members of the BRC's retail credit group holding nearly 14.5 million accounts, the total amount owed at the end of the last quarter was 2.4 billion pounds -- the highest figure recorded for this period and up 22 percent on the same time last year.

"These figures show that store credit is growing in line with other types of consumer credit," said Andrew Sentance, the BRC's chief economic adviser and director of the London Business School's Centre for Economic Forecasting.

"This is not surprising, given the healthy rate of increase in retail sales over the last year. However, consumers are managing their debt sensibly. All the increase is coming from a higher number of cardholders and the amount outstanding on each card is virtually static."
